svg.title: Critical friend: journey through the playbook
svg.desc: Critical friend: journey through the playbook. Stops run across the top in the order they are met, and this reads one stop at a time. Seven steps on one assignment, from being asked to saying what you assured. Stop 1: You have been asked to be a critical friend. In the playbook: The critical friend What you are confirming. What you do there: You give independent advice. You are not delivering the analysis. Outputs: Nothing recorded yet. Watch out for: You and the analyst shall be independent in all cases. Stop 2: How far from the work do I have to sit? In the playbook: The critical friend Independence. What you do there: The separation follows the level, from a colleague to external review. Outputs: Your name on the design and plan, before work starts. Watch out for: Found afterwards, you review what was produced. Named beforehand, you shape it. Stop 3: What am I actually reviewing? In the playbook: Phase 2 Design. What you do there: Review the plan. Confirm the approach and assurance level are right. Outputs: A reviewed assurance plan, and your time in the schedule. Watch out for: A plan with no time in the schedule is only intent. Stop 4: What checks am I doing? In the playbook: The checks, by level. What you do there: Run the checks the level asks for, and the levels inside it. Outputs: Your entries in the quality assurance log. Watch out for: The log records which checks, when, and what you found. Stop 5: I have found something. In the playbook: Phase 3 Analysis. What you do there: You shall review the analyst's assurance and report errors and improvements back. Outputs: Your findings, and the analyst's response to each one. Watch out for: Reporting them is yours. Acting on them is the analyst's. Stop 6: Has the uncertainty been handled honestly? In the playbook: R10 Uncertainty. What you do there: Check assumptions are traceable, and uncertainty quantified where the method allows. Outputs: A recorded view on whether uncertainty is handled adequately. Watch out for: Limitations in the output rather than only in an annex. Stop 7: Saying what I assured. In the playbook: Phase 4 Delivery and sign-off. What you do there: State the assurance: appropriately scoped, executed, validated, verified and documented. Outputs: The quality assurance statement, or your part of it. Watch out for: None. The loop: Step 7 loops back to step 2. What you report back is what the next piece of work avoids. Open alongside, at any step: R8 for what binds the work in front of you. Deciding your assurance level to check the level is right, because assuring to the wrong level is a finding in itself. R2 for the checklist and the log. NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Seamus Sands for NHSBSA, SOW-DOC053.
